chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: NumPy also comes with a bunch of handy functions to generate arrays filled with random values.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: These functions are defined in NumPy's random module.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: The random function generates uniformly sampled floating point values between 0 and 1,

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: with 0 inclusive and 1 exclusive.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: More formally, we can say that it generates values in the half open interval 0.0 and 1.0.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Let's go ahead and print this.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Here is the generated array with 5 rows and 4 columns.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Note that we pass the array shape as a tuple.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: A slightly variant of this function is rand,

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: which directly accepts a sequence of numbers as arguments instead of a tuple.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: It is otherwise equivalent.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Observe that we directly pass the values of the rows and columns to the function and did not define a tuple.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Here it is the array with same shape as before, 5 rows and 4 columns.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: NumPy provides this to achieve a greater compatibility with the more established MATLAB syntax.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: We however recommend using a more consistent NumPy function that explicitly accepts a shape tuple.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Now both the function rand and random sample uniformly from the range 0 and 1.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: What if you wanted to sample from a different distribution?

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: To sample from a Gaussian or normal distribution, we can use the normal function.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: We call the normal function from numpy.random and pass the shape of the array we require.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Let's run this.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: The code produced a 2 into 3 array of random numbers with a standard normal distribution.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: That is 0 mean and unit standard deviation.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: You can change the mean and the standard deviation as well.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Let's see how to do that.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: We change the mean to 50 and standard deviation to 10.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Now let's see the output.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Notice that the values are centered around 50.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: To generate integers, we can use the randint function in one of the several ways.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Passing two values, 0 and 10 will notify randint to generate a single integer between the range 0 and 10.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: We can also specify randint how many integers do we want between 0 and 10 by specifying the size attribute and giving it a value.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: So this statement will give us a 1d array of five integers between the range 0 and 10.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Going forward with that, we can pass a tuple value to the attribute size,

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: which will create a 2d array with all the values between the range 0 and 10.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Now let's see the output.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: These are the single random integers between the range 0 and 10.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Next, we created a 1d array with five values.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Note that we mentioned the number of values needed in the one dimensional array with the parameter size.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Passing a tuple to the size parameter gave us a 2d values.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: And also note that all the values of the array are between 0 and 10.

chunks.title: Generating random numbers
chunks.text: Check out the other random sampling routines on the NumPy website for more distribution and usage variations.
